knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)

```{r}
# Install the local library with: devtools::install("retractionwatch")
# or load it during development with: devtools::load_all("retractionwatch")
# At the moment we are using the development version
devtools::install("retractionwatch")
devtools::load_all("retractionwatch")
# Once the package is installed, you can load it with library(retractionwatch)
# library(retractionwatch)
library(plotly)

# # Loading data

sjr_country_counts <- build_sjr_country_counts("data/sjr_rankings")
oecd_countries <- load_oecd_countries("data/oecd_countries.csv")
retraction_data <- load_retraction_data("data/retraction_watch.csv")

retraction_data <- aggregate_publishers(retraction_data)


# Remove all reasons not grouped as Mechanism
mechanisms_data <- retraction_data %>%
  remove_retraction_reasons(reasons_in_group("Mechanism", invert = TRUE))

# Remove the reasons grouped as Mechanism (e.g. "Investigation by
# Journal/Publisher") but keep their papers, which still count in the totals
retraction_data <- retraction_data %>%
  remove_retraction_reasons(reasons_in_group("Mechanism"))

publication_counts <- publication_counts_by_class(sjr_country_counts, oecd_countries)
retraction_data_nomass <- retraction_data[retraction_data$Mass_Retraction == "Other",]

# The data is filtered by publication year when loaded, but the publishers are
# compared by retraction year, as this page looks at how their retraction
# practices change over time
publisher_year_col <- "retraction_year"

# Check the years of the analysis below
#retraction_data_uk <- retraction_data |>
#  subset(Country == "United Kingdom")
#ggplotly(plot_retraction_reasons_over_time(retraction_data_uk, year_limits = c(2000, 2026), n_top = 2, min_retractions_per_year = 20))

# Country classes are per paper (UK > Other OECD > Rest of World), so the
# two subsets below never share a paper
retraction_data_uk <- retraction_data |>
  subset(country_class == "United Kingdom")
retraction_data_uk_nomass <- retraction_data_uk |>
  subset(Mass_Retraction == "Other")

retraction_data_oecd <- retraction_data |>
  subset(country_class == "Other OECD")
retraction_data_oecd_nomass <- retraction_data_oecd |>
  subset(Mass_Retraction == "Other")
```

# Retractions for the top 10 publishers

```{r}
publisher_and_retractions <- count_number_of_retractions_per_column(
  retraction_data_nomass,
  column_name = "Publisher", year_limits = c(2017, 2026),
  year_col = publisher_year_col)


top_10_publishers <- publisher_and_retractions |>
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 10)

print(top_10_publishers)
```

```{r}
ggplotly(plot_proportion_of_total_retractions_per_publisher(retraction_data_nomass, top_n = 20, year_limits = c(2017, 2026),
                                                            year_col = publisher_year_col))
```

```{r}
ggplotly(ggplot(top_10_publishers,
       aes(x = retractions, y = reorder(Publisher, retractions))) +
  geom_col(fill = "#1b9e77", orientation = "y") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(title = "Top 10 publishers by number of retractions",
       x = "Retractions (excluding mass retractions)",
       y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
)
```

# Retraction mechanisms change over time 

### By retraction year

However, the mechanisms are applied at the time of retractions, so the retraction year is also relevant to understand the changes in retraction practices over time.

####  In all the data

```{r}
mechanisms_per_publisher_and_year <- calculate_proportion_of_retractions_per_year_by_publisher(
  mechanisms_data |> subset(Mass_Retraction == "Other"),
  publisher_list = top_10_publishers,
  yearmin = 2017,
  yearmax = 2026,
  year_col = publisher_year_col)
```

```{r}
plot_reason_proportions_across_groups_by_year(mechanisms_per_publisher_and_year,
interactive = TRUE,
title = "Average proportion of retraction citing each mechanism across 10 publishers with most retractions")
```

Average proportion of retractions citing each reason across the top 10 publishers. The shaded bands show the interquartile range (25th to 75th percentile) across publishers. Each publisher counts the same, whatever its number of retractions, and publishers without retractions in a year are left out of that year.

# Top 10 retraction reasons from 2017 to 2026 for top 10 publishers

Excluding mass retractions

```{r}
top_10_reasons <- select_top_retraction_reasons(retraction_data_nomass, n_top = 10, year_limits = c(2017, 2026),
                                               year_col = publisher_year_col)
```

```{r}
top_10_reasons_per_publisher_and_year <- calculate_proportion_of_retractions_per_year_by_publisher(
  retraction_data_nomass,
  publisher_list = top_10_publishers,
  reasons = top_10_reasons,
  yearmin = 2017,
  yearmax = 2026,
  year_col = publisher_year_col)
```

```{r}
plot_reason_proportions_across_groups_by_year(top_10_reasons_per_publisher_and_year,
interactive = TRUE)
```

# AI retraction reasons from 2017 to 2026 for top 10 publishers

Excluding mass retractions

```{r}
ai_reasons <- c("Computer-Aided Content or Computer-Generated Content")
```

```{r}
ai_reasons_per_publisher_and_year <- calculate_proportion_of_retractions_per_year_by_publisher(
  retraction_data_nomass,
  publisher_list = top_10_publishers,
  reasons = ai_reasons,
  yearmin = 2017,
  yearmax = 2026,
  year_col = publisher_year_col)
```

```{r}
plot_reason_proportions_across_groups_by_year(ai_reasons_per_publisher_and_year,
interactive = TRUE)
```

```{r}
ai_reasons_per_publisher_and_year <- calculate_proportion_of_retractions_per_year_by_publisher(
  retraction_data_nomass,
  publisher_list = top_10_publishers,
  reasons = ai_reasons,
  yearmin = 2017,
  yearmax = 2026,
  year_col = publisher_year_col)
```

```{r}
plots <- lapply(unique(ai_reasons), function(reason) {
ggplotly(ggplot(ai_reasons_per_publisher_and_year |> filter(Reason == reason),
       aes(x = year, y = proportion, colour = Publisher)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(title = reason,
       x = "Retraction year",
       y = "Proportion of retractions",
       colour = "Publisher") +
  theme_minimal()+
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank())
)})
htmltools::tagList(plots)
```

```{r}
ggplotly(plot_reason_proportion_per_publisher(
    retraction_data_nomass,
    reason = "Computer-Aided Content or Computer-Generated Content",
    publisher_list = top_10_publishers,
    year_limits = c(2017, 2026),
    year_col = publisher_year_col,
    confidence_interval = TRUE),
    height = 300
  )
```

## Heterogeneity among top 10 retracted reasons of publishers with most retractions

```{r}
top_10_reasons <- select_top_retraction_reasons(retraction_data_nomass, n_top = 10, year_limits = c(2017, 2026),
                                               year_col = publisher_year_col)

plots <- lapply(top_10_reasons, function(reason) {
ggplotly(plot_reason_proportion_per_publisher(
    retraction_data_nomass,
    reason = reason,
    publisher_list = top_10_publishers,
    year_limits = c(2017, 2026),
    year_col = publisher_year_col,
    confidence_interval = TRUE),
    height = 300
  )
})
htmltools::tagList(plots)
```

# Heterogeneity of the 10 publishers with most retractions

```{r}
print(top_10_publishers)

ggplotly(plot_reason_heterogeneity(retraction_data_nomass, top_10_publishers, top_10_reasons,
                          group_col = "Publisher", year_limits = c(2017, 2026),
                          year_col = publisher_year_col))
```

Proportion of each publisher's retractions citing each reason from 2017 to 2026. The box goes from the first to the third quartile, the thick line is the median and the whiskers reach the most extreme publishers within 1.5 times the interquartile range from the box. Publishers beyond the whiskers are outliers, shown as asterisks; every other publisher is a small point. Hover over a point or asterisk to see the publisher and its counts.

```{r}
ggplotly(plot_reason_proportions_boxplot(retraction_data_nomass, top_10_publishers, top_10_reasons,
                                         group_col = "Publisher", year_limits = c(2017, 2026),
                                         year_col = publisher_year_col),
         tooltip = "text")

```
